Xenosaga Episode I - Der Wille zur Macht () is a role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Namco. It was released in 2002 in Japan and in 2003 in North America for the Sony PlayStation 2. It is the first game released in the series.

Xenosaga Freaks () is a video game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Namco. It was released in 2004 for the Sony PlayStation 2 only in Japan. It is a collection of: * Xeno-comi, a visual novel with a side story that plays during Xenosaga Episode I * Xeno-pittan, a puzzle game somewhat similar to Scrabble * The with entries from Xenosaga Episode I * A Demo for Xenosaga Episode II

Xenosaga I & II (, Xenosaga I・II) is a role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft and Tom Create and published by Namco. It was released in 2006 on the Nintendo DS exclusively in Japan. This game is a retelling of Xenosaga Episode I and Xenosaga Episode II.

Xenosaga: Pied Piper () is a role-playing game developed by Monolith Soft, Namco Mobile and Tom Create and published by Namco. It was released in 2004 exclusively on Japanese mobile phones. It is a prequel that tells the story of Ziggy in his life as the human Jan Sauer, and takes place 100 years before the main events of Xenosaga Episode I and Xenosaga Episode II. A G-MODE version of Xenosaga Pied Piper was released on Steam and Nintendo Switch on .

The Xenoblade Chronicles 2 Kingdom of Torna Original Soundtrack (Xenoblade2: Ougon no Kuni Iira Original Soundtrack, later Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack on Amazon Music and iTunes) is the official soundtrack for Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country. It consists of (almost) all of the music that was featured in this game but not in the Xenoblade Chronicles 2 base game. It was composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, ACE, Kenji Hiramatsu and Manami Kiyota. The soundtrack was initially released only digitally. Later, a physical version of the soundtrack was released as part of the Xenoblade Chronicles Original Soundtrack Trinity Box.
Xeno-pittan (, Word puzzle: Xeno-pittan) is a minigame in Xenosaga Freaks. It is a Xenosaga-themed spinoff of Namco's series.

Xenosaga III: Also Sprach Zarathustra Original Sound Best Tracks is the only official release of the soundtrack of Xenosaga Episode III - Also Sprach Zarathustra, released on 2 CDs in 2006. All tracks were composed by Yuki Kajiura. The album contains only a small portion of the full soundtrack — the sound producer Keiichi Nozaki requested Kajiura to choose 2 discs' worth of tracks, as the full OST would've needed 6 discs to fit all of the music. The ordering of tracks does not seem to correspond to any ordering in which the tracks may play in-game; it is possible that Kajiura simply chose an ordering which she believed to constitute a good listening experience. The Xenosaga THE ANIMATION Original Soundtrack is the official soundtrack for Xenosaga: The Animation. All tracks on the soundtrack were composed by Kousuke Yamashita. It was released on a single CD on the 23rd of March, 2005 under the label Columbia Music Entertainment, in Japan only.

The Xenoblade Chronicles 3 Expansion Pass is a collection of downloadable content for Xenoblade Chronicles 3. The content included cannot be purchased separately. It includes: * Useful items, including accessories. * Cosmetic options that change the main party's clothing appearance. * New Heroes and associated s. * A mode. * Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed, a new story scenario.

Xenosaga: The Animation is a twelve-episode anime series animated by Toei Animation which premiered on TV Asahi in Japan on January 5th, 2005 and on Anime Network in the United States on August 30th, 2007. The anime is based off the events of Xenosaga Episode I, although there are differences.

Xenosaga Episode I Reloaded () is a Japan-exclusive re-release of Xenosaga Episode I - Der Wille zur Macht for the PlayStation 2. It notably includes the English voice acting from the North American release of the original game, along with a few other features. This version is based upon the international version of Xenosaga Episode I that was released in North America in February 25th 2003.

The Xenoblade Chronicles 3 Original Soundtrack is the official soundtrack set for Xenoblade Chronicles 3 and Future Redeemed and the most complete release of the music of this game. It was composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, ACE, Kenji Hiramatsu, Manami Kiyota, Mariam Abounnasr, and Yutaka Kunigo. It includes tracks from the base game and from Volume 4 of the Expansion Pass spread across 9 discs. Two different versions of the soundtrack were released: * Standard edition: This version was released on the 2nd of August, 2023. The Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack is the official soundtrack set for Xenoblade Chronicles Definitive Edition and the most complete release of the music of this game. It was composed by Manami Kiyota, ACE, Kenji Hiramatsu, and Yasunori Mitsuda. It includes all remixes of tracks specific to the Definitive Edition, all tracks which were not remixed for this edition, and the 8 tracks composed for Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. The soundtrack released on the 2nd of August, 2023. The music is also included as part of the Xenoblade Chronicles Original Soundtrack Trinity Box.

The Xenoblade Chronicles Original Soundtrack Trinity Box is a collection of the soundtracks for the numbered Xenoblade Chronicles games: the Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack, the Xenoblade Chronicles 2 Original Sountrack (type C), the Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack, and the Xenoblade Chronicles 3 Original Soundtrack. Notably, the Trinity Box is the only official release of the Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack which released physically on a disc. The Xenosaga Information Device, or X.I.D. for short, was a program distributed at the Xenosaga website around one month before the North American release of Xenosaga Episode I. It was used to distrubute news and exclusive media like artwork, screenshots from the game, short previews from the soundtrack and even a countdown to the Xenosagas release. While it can still be installed and executed on modern iterations of Windows, the servers it tries to connect to have long been discontinued. As of July 2009, it was still available for download.

Xenosaga Another Story (), also referred to as Xenosaga EPISODE II Another Story, is a short-form video series that was uploaded to the official Japanese Xenosaga website in 2004 to promote the release of Xenosaga Episode II. Although the website has since been shut down, the video series was officially preserved in the Xenosaga alle spezielle DVD, distributed as a pre-order bonus for the Japanese release of Xenosaga Episode III. Screenshots of the series were also published in the Episode II issues of the Xenosaga Weekly magazine.
